claim: Lumasiran reduces urinary oxalate in primary hyperoxaluria type 1
gold_rationale: Lumasiran (Oxlumo) is an FDA (24 Nov 2020, NDA214103) and EMA-approved GalNAc-siRNA that silences hepatic glycolate oxidase (HAO1), reducing oxalate overproduction in PH1. The claimed outcome — urinary oxalate — IS the disease driver and the explicit regulatory basis of approval (FDA label: 'to lower urinary and plasma oxalate levels'). The pivotal double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3 ILLUMINATE-A (Garrelfs, NEJM 2021; NCT03681184, N=39) met its primary endpoint: ~65% least-squares mean reduction in 24-h urinary oxalate corrected for BSA vs placebo (adjusted difference ~53 percentage points, p<0.001), with a large fraction normalizing. This was corroborated by the randomized Phase 1/2 study (Frishberg, CJASN 2021; up to ~75% UOx reduction), the ILLUMINATE-A final 60-month results (CJASN 2026; ~54% sustained UOx reduction), and single-arm Phase 3 trials where an RCT could not ethically be run: ILLUMINATE-B in infants/young children <6 yr (72% reduction in spot UOx:creatinine) and ILLUMINATE-C in advanced kidney disease/dialysis (which used PLASMA oxalate as primary because urinary oxalate is unreliable in renal failure). Consensus across the pivotal RCT, confirmatory trials, and regulatory action is unambiguous: Supported. ILLUMINATE-C's primary endpoint is a plasma (not urinary) surrogate in a CKD subset, so it partially matches; it does not contradict.

baseline.text: Yes. Lumasiran (Oxlumo), an RNAi therapeutic that silences hepatic glycolate oxidase (HAO1) to cut oxalate overproduction, clearly reduces urinary oxalate in primary hyperoxaluria type 1. The pivotal Phase 3 placebo-controlled ILLUMINATE-A trial showed roughly a 65% reduction in 24-hour urinary oxalate from baseline (about a 53-percentage-point difference vs placebo), with most treated patients normalizing or near-normalizing urinary oxalate. This was confirmed in infants/young children (ILLUMINATE-B) and supported the FDA/EMA approval in 2020. This is one of the best-established efficacy claims in rare metabolic disease.

rows.citation: Garrelfs SF, et al. Lumasiran, an RNAi Therapeutic for Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1. N Engl J Med. 2021;384(13):1216-1226. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2021712 (ILLUMINATE-A, NCT03681184).
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3; PubMed article types include 'Randomized Controlled Trial' and 'Clinical Trial, Phase III'. Basis of FDA/EMA approval. No retraction. Verified via PubMed get_article_metadata (title/journal/pages/DOI exact) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03681184 primary endpoint = percent change in 24-h urinary oxalate corrected for BSA).
rows.finding: Primary endpoint met: ~65.4% least-squares mean reduction in 24-h urinary oxalate (BSA-corrected) from baseline to month 6 with lumasiran vs ~11.8% with placebo (adjusted difference ~53.5 percentage points, p<0.001); 52% of lumasiran patients reached urinary oxalate at or below normal. Direct urinary-oxalate outcome in PH1. n_int=26 = lumasiran arm; N=39 total enrolled.

rows.citation: Frishberg Y, et al. Phase 1/2 Study of Lumasiran for Treatment of Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1: A Placebo-Controlled Randomized Clinical Trial. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2021;16(7):1025-1036. DOI:10.2215/CJN.14730920 (NCT02706886).
rows.integrity_note: Randomized placebo-controlled Phase 1/2 dose-finding study; PubMed article types include 'Randomized Controlled Trial', 'Clinical Trial, Phase I', 'Clinical Trial, Phase II'. Primary endpoint was safety (AE incidence) with urinary oxalate as a pharmacodynamic outcome — outcome_match=true retained because the claimed outcome (urinary oxalate reduction) was directly measured and strongly positive. Verified via PubMed get_article_metadata.
rows.finding: 20 PH1 patients (+32 healthy in part A): lumasiran produced a mean maximal reduction of ~75% from baseline in 24-h urinary oxalate across dosing cohorts; ALL PH1 patients achieved urinary oxalate <=1.5x ULN (near-normalization). Same direction on the claimed outcome; supported the ILLUMINATE-A dose.

rows.citation: Frishberg Y, Saland JM, Lieske JC, et al. (incl. Sas DJ). Final Results of the ILLUMINATE-A Phase 3 Clinical Trial of Lumasiran for Primary Hyperoxaluria 1. Clin J Am Soc Nephrol. 2026;21(3):377-388. DOI:10.2215/CJN.0000000916 (NCT03681184, 60-month final analysis).
rows.integrity_note: CORRECTED: corpus originally dated this 2024 and led with Sas DJ; actual publication is CJASN 21(3):377-388, March 2026 (PMID:41343248), lead author Frishberg Y. Long-term/extension of the pivotal RCT — ILLUMINATE-A had a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 6-month period followed by open-label extension; placebo group crossed to lumasiran. design=rct retained on the strength of the parent controlled design. Verified via Exa (Ovid/Mayo Clinic Elsevier Pure abstract, PubMed 41343248).
rows.finding: Final 60-month ILLUMINATE-A analysis: sustained ~54% reduction in 24-h urinary oxalate at month 60 in both the lumasiran/lumasiran and placebo/lumasiran groups; plasma oxalate down ~35-38%; eGFR stable, reduced kidney stone event rates, improved nephrocalcinosis. Durable urinary-oxalate lowering.

rows.citation: Hayes W, Sas DJ, et al. Efficacy and safety of lumasiran for infants and young children with primary hyperoxaluria type 1: 12-month analysis of the phase 3 ILLUMINATE-B trial. Pediatr Nephrol. 2022;38(4):1075-1086. DOI:10.1007/s00467-022-05684-1 (NCT03905694).
rows.integrity_note: CORRECTED design: open-label SINGLE-ARM Phase 3 (no placebo, ethically justified in infants <6 yr) — PubMed article types show 'Clinical Trial, Phase III' but NO 'Randomized Controlled Trial' tag, so reclassified from 'rct' to 'prospective cohort' (single-arm interventional). Primary endpoint IS spot urinary oxalate:creatinine (outcome_match=true). Verified via PubMed get_article_metadata + Exa (PMC9925547, Alnylam PR).
rows.finding: Infants/young children <6 yr (N=18): ~72% least-squares-mean reduction in spot urinary oxalate:creatinine ratio at month 6 (95% CI 66.4-77.5%), maintained at 72% through month 12 (89%/68%/71% across <10/10-20/>=20 kg weight subgroups); plasma oxalate also fell (32%->47%). Confirms the urinary-oxalate effect in the youngest PH1 patients.

rows.citation: Michael M, et al. Lumasiran for Advanced Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1: Phase 3 ILLUMINATE-C Trial. Am J Kidney Dis. 2022;81(2):145-155. DOI:10.1053/j.ajkd.2022.05.012 (NCT04152200).
rows.integrity_note: CORRECTED design: open-label SINGLE-ARM Phase 3 in advanced CKD/dialysis — PubMed article types show 'Clinical Trial, Phase III' but NO 'Randomized Controlled Trial' tag, so reclassified from 'rct' to 'prospective cohort'. PRIMARY endpoint is PLASMA oxalate (surrogate substitution: urinary oxalate is unreliable in renal failure/dialysis); urinary oxalate measured only as secondary -> outcome_match=false (correct). Population is a severe CKD subset (population_match=true, still PH1). Verified via PubMed get_article_metadata + Exa.
rows.finding: Advanced kidney disease incl. hemodialysis (N=21): plasma oxalate fell ~33% (cohort A, not on HD) and ~42% (cohort B, on HD) at month 6; secondary spot urinary oxalate:creatinine also improved. Consistent direction, but the CLAIMED outcome (urinary oxalate) is only a secondary endpoint here — primary is a plasma surrogate.

rows.citation: Kang C. Lumasiran: A Review in Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1. Drugs. 2024;84(2):219-226. DOI:10.1007/s40265-023-01987-1 (PMC10981577).
rows.integrity_note: CORRECTED CITATION: corpus fabricated the authorship/year as 'Scott LJ, Keam SJ. Drugs 2023;83(8):733-740'; the DOI is real but resolves to Kang C, Drugs 2024;84(2):219-226 (Adis Drug Evaluation, open access, PMC10981577). Secondary synthesis, not primary data (n_int=0). Verified via Exa (Springer Nature Link + PMC).
rows.finding: Adis review of the full ILLUMINATE program: in double-blind placebo-controlled ILLUMINATE-A, lumasiran was significantly more effective than placebo in reducing 24-h urinary oxalate (aged >=6 yr), sustained through 36 months; single-arm ILLUMINATE-B reduced urinary oxalate:creatinine and plasma oxalate in <6 yr; single-arm ILLUMINATE-C reduced plasma oxalate in dialysis and non-dialysis patients. FDA/EMA approved. Reflects established consensus that lumasiran reduces urinary oxalate in PH1.

provenance: Re-verified independently. PubMed get_article_metadata confirmed titles/journals/pages/DOIs/article-types for PMIDs 33789010, 33985991, 35913563, 35843439 (checked for 'Retracted Publication' — none). ClinicalTrials.gov get_trial_details NCT03681184 confirmed Phase 3 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled, N=39, primary endpoint = percent change in 24-h urinary oxalate corrected for BSA. Exa web_search verified the two DOI-only rows: DOI:10.2215/CJN.0000000916 = Frishberg et al., CJASN 21(3):377-388 (2026, PMID:41343248); DOI:10.1007/s40265-023-01987-1 = Kang C, Drugs 84(2):219-226 (2024, PMC10981577). FDA approval date confirmed 24 Nov 2020 (Alnylam PR + DailyMed NDA214103, label indicates lowering urinary and plasma oxalate). Per PubMed terms: based on articles retrieved from PubMed; DOIs included.
notes: 6 verified rows survive; defensible gold consensus -> status='revised'. Two citation errors fixed (Row 3 year 2024->2026 + lead author + PMID added; Row 6 fabricated Scott/Keam citation replaced with the real Kang C 2024 review that the DOI resolves to). Two single-arm Phase 3 trials (ILLUMINATE-B, -C) reclassified from 'rct' to 'prospective cohort' per PubMed article-type check (no RCT tag). No hallucinated PMIDs, no wrong effect directions, no fabricated retractions, no wrong N (n_int values checked: 26 lumasiran arm of 39, 20, 39, 18, 21, 0). No conflicting trial wrongly marked population_match=false — all rows are genuine PH1 and none contradict the claim. ILLUMINATE-C outcome_match=false correctly flags its plasma-oxalate surrogate primary endpoint. dramatic_effect=false correct throughout (pivotal evidence is a proper placebo-controlled RCT, not all-or-none).
